renderMode.help: ASCII draws the eyes out of colored glyphs. PNG uses the photographic frames — lighter on CPU, and it starts instantly.

scale.help: How much of the screen the eyes fill. Past 100% they overflow and the edges are cropped.

tintEnabled.help: Off leaves the default ember red. On replaces it with the color below.

tintColor.help: Only the hue is used — the eyes keep their own black shadows and white-hot cores.

tintStrength.help: How far the color pulls away from gray. Needs Custom color switched on.

glowAuto.help: Picks the bloom strength that suits the current render mode. Turn off to set it yourself.

glow.help: Bloom strength. Needs Auto glow switched off.

trackMouse.help: Needs mouse input enabled in Lively's own settings. Mutually exclusive with Follow the webcam.

trackWebcam.help: Uses your camera to track face position. Mutually exclusive with Follow the cursor. First-time setup: hide desktop icons (right-click desktop → View), then use the on-screen setup panel. Allow camera for Lively in Windows Settings → Privacy → Camera.

autoBlink.help: Blink every 3 to 5 seconds, on their own.

idleDrowsySec.help: Seconds of no cursor activity before the eyes go half-closed. 0 keeps them awake.

fpsCap.help: 30 roughly halves the CPU cost. Uncapped follows your display's refresh rate.
